title: At the Table: DHS resources that help Veterans build a future in homeland security
summary:
Across the country, many Veterans are choosing homeland security as their next mission. The leadership, discipline, and technical skills Veterans developed in uniform translate naturally to work that protects the nation’s people, borders, infrastructure, and waterways. As the Department of Homeland Security undergoes major modernization efforts and expands its workforce, Veterans are stepping forward as the next generation of national security professionals.

In the latest episode of At the Table, VA Deputy Secretary Paul R. Lawrence, Ph.D., talks with Deputy Secretary of Homeland Security Troy Edgar about the opportunities available to Veterans at DHS. Their conversation highlights why Veterans are well prepared for careers in homeland security, how DHS is growing across multiple mission areas, and what resources are available to help Veterans navigate the transition.

Deputy Secretary Edgar explains that DHS currently has almost 30,000 open positions across 23 mission components. These components include law enforcement, maritime security, emergency management, cybersecurity, transportation security, and immigration services. Approximately 30 percent of DHS’s 260,000 employees are already Veterans. DHS has long recognized that Veterans bring mission focus, teamwork, responsibility, and an ability to perform under pressure. A career at DHS allows many Veterans to continue serving their country in a new capacity. 

Veterans can explore these opportunities at the DHS careers site: https://www.dhs.gov/homeland-security-careers.
